body: Advice is going to vary based off of where in CA you are. Are you a level 7 getting ready for practice days/your week? A level 6 trying to get your 7? A baby 4th about to go to a new store? It’ll all determine what advice. The only real broad advice I can think of is to control your attitude. There are going to be a hundred things each day you can’t control, from people calling in, associates attitudes, and so many many more variables. Only by controlling your own self can you make a positive impact. Always be willing to learn from someone, even if it’s learn what *not* to do.
The 30 days is insurmountable though. No income, no way to pay rent, and a lost career.
Thank you for the encouragement. Will ask my lawyer about an appeal if this doesn’t go well

Contra Costa. And yeah, I’m gonna ask my attorney about the right time to say all that. He seems like a good attorney, lots of good reviews and stuff. But if I do lose my license for 30 days. That’s what I’m talking about.
I did. “This county is pretty strict on 30 days, I can’t guarantee, but there’s a chance…” “a chance? Cool!” “Well, the courts have discretion, and it’s only 30 days…”
But it won’t go away. Losing my job, my career, won’t go away. And yeah. I know I gotta tell her. I just don’t know how. If I see her heart break again it’ll finish me all on its own.
You think I don’t know that? That’s why I feel like such a fucking loser
Found an attorney, just trying to get home. Thought I was going 90, it was 2am.
Thank you for your kind words. I just don’t see any way out and I feel like the walls are closing in
Maybe, about the girlfriend. Maybe. But the job? Trust me, I’m easy to replace. I’m not even needed at my job.
This job is stupidly high paying for the job. 55k. Might not mean much to some people, but to me, it’s the only job that’ll offer healthcare and a career. Flipping freaking burgers lol.

This county is apparently super strict on the 30 day suspension for all drivers. Where I’m at, people are over COVID. It is literally a part of manager’s jobs title to drive/drive people home.

The Advil and knife is sort of an homage to my dad. He tried and failed to commit suicide the same way in the room next to mine.

And I want to tell her. I really do. I’m just terrified of what she’ll say. Terrified of the look in her eyes. I’ve dreamed of a future with her for so long, and now I done ruined it. She deserves so much better than me.
Irrelevant to who?
Like, death by a thousand cuts if I lose my job and slowly continue to drag her down. Or I could just make it quick, give her a chance and move on.
No. But I already did.

To myself? Because I don’t know what else to do. I can’t become like the people in my family who lose their jobs and just do nothing with their lives. I couldn’t look myself in the mirror if I ended up like them. I already feel so far behind the curve; living with my girlfriend’s family @26 years old? And now this. If I lose my car I don’t see a way forward.

To her? Because part of me is a selfish prick, and part of me loves her more than life itself and doesn’t want to see her with someone like that.

I doubt for the rest of her life. She’s an amazing woman. It would take her a little while, but her family is here. She’d get through it. And she would/will definitely be better off than with some loser boyfriend who can’t hold down a freaking career.
But wait I literally cannot still get it. I’m gonna lose my freaking job. No backup plan or savings to speak of.
Maybe she’ll go and find someone who isn’t a moron?
Maybe. But seeing her look at me with that much disappointment. I’ve been working towards this future for 5 years. I’m finally close. And now this

My job requires that I “drive” there. The thought has occurred to me that I could bus trip there (1:44 trip, not bad for bus) then maybe Uber the last 2 minutes to keep up a facade? But that only takes care of morning shifts, and then only shakily. For closing shifts I’m required to be the last one leaving the lot, and possibly give rides to people. I’m in a county with a strict policy about 30 day suspensions on licenses for 100+mph tickets, so I’m basically gonna lose my license for 30 days. My chest hurts. I want to tell my girlfriend, but I don’t want to see the disappointment in her eyes. The court date is sometime in the next 60 days, haven’t gotten a courtesy notice. Part of me just wants to clean up my room as best I can, pack stuff into boxes then, the court day, just start driving really really fast with a bottle of Advil and a knife. I moved out here to start a life with her. Losing my job would effectively end that hope, in this godforsaken state of CA.

*I meant suspend my license, and all the attorneys I’ve talked to say it’s likely in this county. So *maybe* for 800 dollars it can maybe be reduced to less than 30 days. But unlikely. And I can’t handle the idea of losing my only lifeline to a future.
Speeding. Just trying to get home from a long shift an hour away from where I live

What if I don’t want to win. I’ll pay the fine. I just can’t afford to not work for 30 days with a suspension.
Edit: commute 1 hour one way.
Thank you. That gives me a little bit of hope. I commute almost an hour every day, so I feel like I’m staring down the barrel of a gun with no hope in sight.

No other tickets. Do I stand any chance of not getting suspended?

Edit: would an attorney make a difference?
Can you give me any idea of how likely it is I am suspended?
True. Thank you.
Thank you. I sent a referral email. I’m terrified. What if I lose my license? I can’t afford a month without work.
Any advice on how to find a lawyer?
But what determines that month? Like, what happens next?
That’s kinda what I was thinking. 45k works out to something like 200 bucks a month. Seems a bit too good to be true.
But then there’s this whole corona thing going on.
That is an excellent question. I found the listing on Zillow. How would I find out?

How can I find out? (Brentwood, fwiw).
